messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're planning to trim cold infra-prod logs from 365d -> 90d starting next month. This will affect SIEM export consumers and the KMS unwrap workflow, so I want to align on the approval model and audit trail.
jon: Do we have an inventory of who currently pulls the exported bundles? Also what KMS changes are we making?
lee: KMS change: moving to per-tenant CMKs with keywrap for exported bundles. That implies a new grant/unlock flow (short-lived unwrap grants) rather than broad, long-lived keys.
nash (ash): Major question: who is allowed to request an unwrapped export? Current entitlement is too wide. We should narrow to specific roles and require justification.
maria: Proposed pattern: (1) short-term lease (7d) for triage analysts, (2) provable legal-hold path (ticket + eDiscovery sign-off), (3) partner exports only via signed job that runs redaction first.
nana (ana): For incidents we need faster access. Can we have an emergency bypass with post-hoc attestation (5-person oncall attest) so responders aren't blocked?
lee: That makes sense. We can implement emergency bypass but it must auto-create a high-fidelity audit entry and alert the security channel.
devops-bot: deploy scheduled: retention-policy-update -> infra-prod on 2026-04-12T03:00Z (no downtime).
jon: Also consider offering masked/partial exports by default (PII redaction) to reduce unwrap needs. Partners can request full export with stronger justification.
lee: Redaction pipeline adds CPU/latency cost but reduces blast radius. We'll need a partner SLA for turnaround.
nash (ash): For RBAC, I propose splitting the single "SIEM-export" permission into two roles: "export-requester" (can request + attach ticket) and "export-reviewer" (approves unwrap). No single person should be able to both request and approve.
maria: Agreed. For emergency bypass, the attestation log must contain oncall IDs, timestamp, and reason. I'll draft the enforcement hooks.
jon: Audit logging requirement: every unwrap must record CMK key-id, grant-id, ticket-id, requester, approver(s), and a free-text justification. Keep those unwrap audit entries for 3 years.
lee: Ack. We'll add structured fields to the audit event so it's queryable in SIEM: {cmk,grant,ticket,requester,approvers,reason}.
nash (ash): Let's also enforce that partner exports default to redacted mode unless a reviewer explicitly toggles full-unwrap and attaches a signed legal form.
maria: I'll open a PR with the migration plan, RBAC changes, and backfill scripts for existing leases. It will include integration tests for the KMS grant lifecycle and an example export payload. Tagging infra and legal for review — @legal-team please advise on the legal-hold flow.
jon: Ping when PR is up. Also we should schedule a dry-run export with a synthetic dataset to validate the audit trail and alerting.
lee: I'll own the dry-run. Recommend running it in staging with the per-tenant CMK emulation.
nash (ash): +1
maria: Example export request payload I'll add to the PR for folks to iterate on:
```json
{
  "requester": "maria",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "ttl_days": 7,
  "reason": "vuln triage #1234",
  "ticket_id": "SEC-1234"
}
```
nana (ana): :thumbsup: Looks good.
maria: If no objections, propose merge on Thursday and enable the 90d retention in infra-prod the following week.
lee: :eyes:
jon: :+1:
